description:
Follow-up to https://github.com/firefly-engineering/toolbox/issues/7.

go-toolchain ships golangci-lint as upstream's prebuilt binary, so the Go it was built with is whatever upstream used, not the toolchain's `go` pin. golangci-lint refuses to lint a module whose `go` directive exceeds its build Go ("the Go language version (go1.26) used to build golangci-lint is lower than the targeted Go version (1.27)"), and on Linux it also fails type-checking a newer GOROOT stdlib (`splice_linux.go: unknown field rfd`).

go-toolchain 7 avoids this only by luck: golangci-lint 2.15.0 happens to be built with go1.27.0 and the toolchain pins go 1.27.2. The next Go minor bump that lands before a matching golangci-lint release recreates the bug, and nothing catches it.

## Options

- Build golangci-lint from source with `toolboxLib.buildGoPackage`, pinned to `versionData.go`, so the toolchain's Go and golangci-lint's build Go are the same by construction. Matches the issue's stated expectation.
- Or keep the prebuilt binary and add a gate: a check that runs `golangci-lint version` (or `go version -m`) for each go-toolchain version and fails when its build Go's language version is below the toolchain's `go` pin.

## Acceptance

- A go-toolchain version cannot be added whose golangci-lint was built with an older Go language version than its `go` component.
- Reproduction: a module with `go 1.<toolchain minor>` lints cleanly in the toolchain's shell, on Linux and macOS, with a fresh GOLANGCI_LINT_CACHE.
title: go-toolchain: guarantee golangci-lint is built with the toolchain's Go
